title: Adaptive Eval Thresholds and Rollback Simulator for Staged Deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current canary / shadow rollout gating uses static thresholds on eval scorecards derived from a small set of reference prompts. These static gates generate two kinds of problems: (1) noise sensitivity — frequent false alarms for low-traffic customers or bursty prompt distributions, and (2) brittle thresholds when models change architecture/quantization, causing either too many rollbacks or unsafe flips.

Goal: Build an adaptive thresholding mechanism plus a rollout simulator that estimates gate false-positive / false-negative behavior for a proposed model variant before traffic is shifted. The system should: 1) derive per-customer baseline distributions for each eval metric using EWMA and windowed percentiles, 2) compute context-aware thresholds that scale with sample count and metric variance, and 3) run a simulator that replays historical golden prompt sets and shadow traffic to estimate expected gating outcomes and economic impact (tokens lost, rollback probability).

Why this is important: Reduces noisy rollbacks, improves developer confidence during staged deployments, and provides quantified trade-offs (sensitivity vs. missed regressions) to PMs and SREs. This complements existing scorecards and sentinel alarms by adding an empirical preflight check and per-customer calibration.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive-threshold service emits per-customer thresholds for all configured eval metrics and persists them to rollout config store
Rollback simulator runs as a pre-deploy job and produces a report (expected false-positive rate, expected missed-regressions, cost delta) for a proposed model build
Console UI surfaces simulator report and recommended traffic split (canary %, shadow %) in the rollout creation flow
End-to-end test: simulated canary using historical shadow capture triggers rollback when simulator predicted >50% false-negative risk
Performance: threshold computation must finish within 30s for customers with up to 1M events in the window (batch processing acceptable)
implementation_notes: Data: extend eval-events table to tag events with customer_id, prompt_bucket, and metric_vector (serialized). Backfill last 90 days for high-traffic customers (batch job).

Algorithm: use a hybrid approach — EWMA for real-time baseline and bootstrap percentile estimation for windows > 100 samples. For low-sample customers (<100 samples) fall back to cohort baselines with a shrinkage factor.

Simulator: replay layer will accept a model_artifact_id and request a dry-run inference from the candidate model in shadow mode; results are compared to historical golden prompt labels and scoring functions. Replay will estimate token cost and time-to-detect metrics.
Config: rollout-config will gain fields: threshold_source (adaptive|static), confidence_level, min_samples, simulator_required (bool).
APIs: new internal endpoints: /v1/thresholds/{customer_id}, /v1/simulate-rollout and webhook for simulator-complete events to the console.
Observability: add Prometheus exporters for threshold computation latency, simulator job durations, and matcher precision/recall estimates.
test_plan: Unit tests for EWMA and bootstrap percentile estimator across synthetic distributions (heavy tails, multimodal).
Integration test: run simulator on archived canary from 2025-11 with a known regression and verify simulator warns of >80% detection chance at recommended settings.
Load test: threshold service handles 200 concurrent customer requests; stress test batch backfill using a k8s job.
Canary: enable adaptive thresholds for internal 'alpha' customers only; monitor false-positive rate vs baseline for two weeks before broader rollout.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Deploy threshold computation service behind feature flag, start continuous backfill jobs for last-90d. Enable simulator in dry-run mode (no console integration).
Week 2: Run simulator for next two queued model builds; gather engineering feedback and refine shrinkage parameters for low-sample customers.
Week 3: Expose simulator reports in Console for internal users; enable adaptive thresholds for 'alpha' tenants and observe metrics for 14 days.
Week 4: Gradual expansion to 20% of canaries; enable automatic suggested traffic splits. Full rollout gated on observed reduction in noisy rollbacks and no increase in missed-regressions.
Rollback policy: simulator recommendation can set 'block' (fail canary creation), 'suggest' (console shows recommended split) or 'no-op'. Only 'block' requires an approval flow.
